segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine.
segments.zh: 我叫 Catherine。

segments.en: And today we've got a very interesting lesson for you all about building your vocabulary.
segments.zh: 今天，我们为大家提供了一个非常有趣的课程，关于构建您的词汇。

segments.en: So we're trying to describe personalities.
segments.zh: 所以我们试图描述个性。

segments.en: You're going to learn tons of new words.
segments.zh: 你会学到大量的新单词。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And as you said, we're going to describe people's personalities.
segments.zh: 正如你所说，我们将描述人们的个性。

segments.en: So not their physical attributes.
segments.zh: 所以不是他们的物理属性。

segments.en: We're going to concentrate on how they are personality wise and stuff like that.
segments.zh: 我们将专注于他们的个性和类似的东西。

segments.en: Their character.
segments.zh: 他们的性格。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So let's take a listen to today's dialogue for the first time and we'll be back in a moment to talk about some of these great words.
segments.zh: 所以让我们第一次听听今天的对话，我们稍后会回来谈谈这些伟大的词。

segments.en: Okay, class, settle down.
segments.zh: 好了，同学们，安静下来。

segments.en: I have the results of your individual personality tests.
segments.zh: 我有你个人性格测试的结果。

segments.en: I'm going to hand them out and if you'd like, you can read them out loud to the rest of the class.
segments.zh: 我要分发它们，如果你愿意，你可以大声朗读它们给班上的其他人。

segments.en: I'll read mine.
segments.zh: 我会读我的。

segments.en: Okay, go ahead.
segments.zh: 好的，继续。

segments.en: It says here that I am adventurous, outgoing and easygoing.
segments.zh: 它在这里说我喜欢冒险、外向和随和。

segments.en: It says that I'm a little superstitious and occasionally naive.
segments.zh: 它说我有点迷信，偶尔也很天真。

segments.en: That's not true.
segments.zh: 那不是真的。

segments.en: Well, the test isn't 100% accurate.
segments.zh: 好吧，测试不是 100% 准确的。

segments.en: Is that all it says?
segments.zh: 这就是它所说的一切吗？

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: It also says that I'm open minded with great ambition, but that I can also be reckless and clumsy.
segments.zh: 它还说我心胸开阔，有着远大的野心，但我也可以鲁莽和笨拙。

segments.en: This is stupid.
segments.zh: 这太蠢了。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Anyone else want to read theirs?
segments.zh: 还有人想读他们的吗？

segments.en: I'll go.
segments.zh: 我来读吧。

segments.en: It says that I'm an extroverted, well balanced person.
segments.zh: 上面说我是个外向、性格稳重的人。

segments.en: It says I am generous, outspoken and very diligent.
segments.zh: 它说我很慷慨，直言不讳，非常勤奋。

segments.en: This is so true.
segments.zh: 这是真的。

segments.en: It also says that I am a magnanimous, eloquent and daring.
segments.zh: 它还说我是一个宽宏大量、雄辩和大胆的人。

segments.en: This is totally me.
segments.zh: 这完全是我。

segments.en: Whatever.
segments.zh: 随便吧。

segments.en: These tests are baloney.
segments.zh: 这些测试是胡说八道。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So we're going to divide this up into language takeaway parts one and two.
segments.zh: 所以我们将把它划分为语言外卖第一部分和第二部分。

segments.en: So let's start with five key words now on language takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以让我们从现在的语言外卖的五个关键词开始。

segments.en: Language takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: The first adjective that came up was adventurous and outgoing.
segments.zh: 出现的第一个形容词是冒险和外向的。

segments.en: Outgoing, that's a good one.
segments.zh: 外向，这是一件好事。

segments.en: Outgoing is a great one.
segments.zh: 外向是一件很棒的事情。

segments.en: So think of the word out.
segments.zh: 所以想想这个词。

segments.en: That means moving out, going out.
segments.zh: 这意味着搬出去，出去。

segments.en: Outgoing means someone is very comfortable talking to strangers or talking to people that they don't know very well.
segments.zh: 外向意味着有人非常自在地与陌生人交谈或与他们不太了解的人交谈。

segments.en: For example, my brother is very outgoing.
segments.zh: 例如，我的兄弟很外向。

segments.en: He loves meeting new people.
segments.zh: 他喜欢结识新朋友。

segments.en: He loves starting conversations with strangers.
segments.zh: 他喜欢与陌生人开始对话。

segments.en: So the opposite would be shy.
segments.zh: 所以相反的会很害羞。

segments.en: That's the opposite.
segments.zh: 那是相反的。

segments.en: Okay, so outgoing.
segments.zh: 好吧，太外向了。

segments.en: And then it also described this person as being a little superstitious.
segments.zh: 然后它还形容这个人有点迷信。

segments.en: Okay, superstitious is very interesting because it's hard to describe since everyone's superstitions are different.
segments.zh: 好吧，迷信很有趣，因为很难描述，因为每个人的迷信都是不同的。

segments.en: In many cultures, there are different superstitions.
segments.zh: 在许多文化中，有不同的迷信。

segments.en: So for example, in America, we say that walking under a ladder is bad luck.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，在美国，我们说在梯子下行走是厄运。

segments.en: Or opening an umbrella inside is bad luck.
segments.zh: 或者在里面打开雨伞是厄运。

segments.en: So if you believe that your actions will bring you bad luck, you're probably superstitious.
segments.zh: 所以如果你相信你的行为会给你带来厄运，你可能是迷信的。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So if you are superstitious, you believe in superstitions.
segments.zh: 因此，如果你是迷信的，你就会相信迷信。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So Marco, are you superstitious?
segments.zh: 所以马可，你迷信吗？

segments.en: Do you think that black cats bring bad luck?
segments.zh: 你认为黑猫会带来厄运吗？

segments.en: No, not at all.
segments.zh: 不，完全没有。

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: That's very interesting.
segments.zh: 这很有趣。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And this is also an interesting word, a way to describe people who are very believing, a person that is naive.
segments.zh: 这也是一个有趣的词，一种描述非常相信的人的方式，一个天真的人。

segments.en: Okay, you said this already.
segments.zh: 好吧，你已经说过了。

segments.en: Naive means that someone generally believes most things that you tell them.
segments.zh: 幼稚的意思是有人通常相信你告诉他们的大多数事情。

segments.en: So if I told you, Marco, hey, did you know that it's supposed to rain frogs tomorrow?
segments.zh: 所以如果我告诉你，马可，嘿，你知道明天应该会下雨吗？

segments.en: No way.
segments.zh: 不会吧。

segments.en: Really?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: Yeah, really.
segments.zh: 是的，真的。

segments.en: If Marco believes me, he's naive.
segments.zh: 如果马可相信我，他很天真。

segments.en: That means that probably it's not going to rain frogs tomorrow, but he believes everything I say.
segments.zh: 这意味着明天可能不会下雨蛙，但他相信我所说的一切。

segments.en: So he's a little bit naive or inexperienced.
segments.zh: 所以他有点天真或缺乏经验。

segments.en: So naive is not really a bad way of describing a person, is it?
segments.zh: 所以天真并不是描述一个人的坏方式，是吗？

segments.en: No, but it can be.
segments.zh: 不，但可以。

segments.en: So you want to be careful.
segments.zh: 所以你要小心。

segments.en: Some people, if you say that they're being naive, it's offensive.
segments.zh: 有些人，如果你说他们很天真，那是令人反感的。

segments.en: So you have to be careful when you say this.
segments.zh: 所以说这话的时候一定要小心。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Moving on, we also had an interesting adjective that described another person, and it was to be reckless.
segments.zh: 继续前进，我们还有一个有趣的形容词，描述了另一个人，这是鲁莽的。

segments.en: I can also be reckless.
segments.zh: 我也可以鲁莽。

segments.en: Reckless.
segments.zh: 鲁莽。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So someone who is reckless often does things without thinking, sometimes things that are dangerous.
segments.zh: 所以一个鲁莽的人经常不假思索地做事，有时是危险的事情。

segments.en: For example, Marco, I think that driving a car without wearing your seatbelt is very reckless.
segments.zh: 例如，Marco，我认为在不系安全带的情况下驾驶汽车是非常鲁莽的。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: That means that you're not thinking about safety.
segments.zh: 这意味着你没有考虑安全。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So a person that is reckless is a kind of a synonym of being a little bit dangerous to be around.
segments.zh: 所以一个鲁莽的人是一种同义词，在周围有点危险。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So someone who does things without thinking about their consequences, their results.
segments.zh: 所以一个人在不考虑他们的后果和结果的情况下做事。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And also along with reckless, the test said that this person was clumsy.
segments.zh: 还有鲁莽，测试说这个人很笨拙。

segments.en: Oh, I love this word.
segments.zh: 哦，我喜欢这个词。

segments.en: There was a very famous commercial when I was growing up in America on the television.
segments.zh: 当我在美国的电视上长大时，有一个非常著名的广告。

segments.en: It was all about young students at high school who are clumsy, and so they should buy this special folder for their schoolwork to help them because they're so clumsy.
segments.zh: 这都是关于高中的年轻学生，他们很笨拙，所以他们应该买这个特殊的文件夹作为他们的功课来帮助他们，因为他们很笨拙。

segments.en: And they're dropping their papers and their books.
segments.zh: 他们正在丢弃他们的论文和书籍。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So someone who is clumsy often falls down or hits their head or trips or drops their things.
segments.zh: 因此，笨拙的人经常跌倒或撞到他们的头或绊倒或掉落他们的东西。

segments.en: If I drop something on the floor and break it, my mother might say, you're so clumsy.
segments.zh: 如果我把东西扔在地板上并打破它，我妈妈可能会说，你太笨拙了。

segments.en: Clumsy fingers.
segments.zh: 笨拙的手指。

segments.en: You should be more careful.
segments.zh: 你应该更加小心。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So clumsy, is this insulting if you say, oh, you're so clumsy?
segments.zh: 太笨拙了，如果你说，哦，你这么笨拙，这是否是侮辱性的？

segments.en: No, it's not so bad.
segments.zh: 不，这不是那么糟糕。

segments.en: There are worse things to say.
segments.zh: 有更糟糕的事情要说。

segments.en: But if someone often drops things, you can call them clumsy.
segments.zh: 但如果有人经常丢东西，你可以称他们为笨拙。

segments.en: Or you can also say, you're such a butterfingers.
segments.zh: 或者你也可以说，你是这样的黄油手指。

segments.en: Butterfingers.
segments.zh: 黄油手指。

segments.en: That means that your fingers are like butter.
segments.zh: 这意味着你的手指就像黄油。

segments.en: They're very slippery.
segments.zh: 它们非常滑。

segments.en: You drop everything.
segments.zh: 你放弃一切。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So clumsy and reckless, they are negative adjectives, right?
segments.zh: 如此笨拙和鲁莽，它们是负面的形容词，对吧？

segments.en: They're saying that you do things wrong.
segments.zh: 他们说你做错事。

segments.en: So it's not really a good thing to be reckless or clumsy.
segments.zh: 所以鲁莽或笨拙并不是一件好事。

segments.en: No, it's not really a good thing.
segments.zh: 不，这不是一件好事。

segments.en: These are not positive characteristics.
segments.zh: 这些不是积极的特征。

segments.en: Okay, good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So we took a look at those five, which are very good about one of the people that took the test.
segments.zh: 所以我们看看这五个，它们对参加考试的人之一非常好。

segments.en: Let's move on now to more language and more adjectives on Language Takeaway part two.
segments.zh: 现在让我们继续讨论更多的语言和更多的语言外卖第二部分。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Alright, so in this part, we're going to take a look at positive attributes about a person, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，在这部分，我们将看看一个人的积极属性，对吧？

segments.en: They're all good things about someone.
segments.zh: 它们都是关于某人的好东西。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And this first one is very good.
segments.zh: 而第一个非常好。

segments.en: Extroverted, extroverted.
segments.zh: 外向，外向。

segments.en: A person that's extroverted.
segments.zh: 一个外向的人。

segments.en: So a synonym of this word is outgoing.
segments.zh: 所以这个词的同义词是外向的。

segments.en: Okay, so it's pretty much the same thing.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这几乎是一回事。

segments.en: That's right, because extra means going out, out.
segments.zh: 没错，因为额外的意味着出去，出去。

segments.en: So in this case, someone who is extroverted often meets new people, goes out and does social things, goes to the movies, goes out with friends, meets strangers, talks to strangers.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，一个外向的人经常结识新朋友，出去做社交活动，去看电影，和朋友出去，遇到陌生人，和陌生人交谈。

segments.en: Again, it's like being outgoing.
segments.zh: 同样，这就像外向。

segments.en: Someone who's comfortable with new people.
segments.zh: 对新朋友感到舒服的人。

segments.en: And what about the opposite?
segments.zh: 而相反的呢？

segments.en: So we said that shy is the opposite of outgoing.
segments.zh: 所以我们说害羞是外向的对立面。

segments.en: What would be the opposite for extroverted?
segments.zh: 外向者的反面是什么？

segments.en: Extroverted's opposite is introverted.
segments.zh: 外向的对立面是内向的。

segments.en: Intro means in, not out.
segments.zh: 介绍意味着进，而不是出。

segments.en: So that means someone who's very shy, who is uncomfortable with new people.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着一个非常害羞，对新人感到不舒服的人。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And well, apart from being extroverted, the test also said that this person is very diligent.
segments.zh: 好吧，除了外向，测试还说这个人很勤奋。

segments.en: Ooh, diligent is a great word.
segments.zh: 哦，勤奋是一个伟大的词。

segments.en: This is a word you want to hear from your teachers and your bosses.
segments.zh: 这是您想从老师和老板那里听到的一个词。

segments.en: Okay, if someone says, Marco, you're very diligent at work.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果有人说，马可，你在工作中很勤奋。

segments.en: What does that mean?
segments.zh: 那是什么意思？

segments.en: It means you're very careful.
segments.zh: 这意味着你非常小心。

segments.en: You always do things very thoroughly.
segments.zh: 你总是非常彻底地做事。

segments.en: And also quickly, right?
segments.zh: 而且还快，对吧？

segments.en: When you tell them to do something, they do it immediately.
segments.zh: 当你告诉他们做某事时，他们会立即做。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So a diligent worker always does a good job and does it in a timely manner.
segments.zh: 所以一个勤奋的工人总是做得很好，并及时做。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And moving on to our third adjective.
segments.zh: 并继续我们的第三个形容词。

segments.en: This one is kind of strange.
segments.zh: 这一种有点奇怪。

segments.en: It kind of sounds like monogamy, but it's magnanimous.
segments.zh: 这听起来像一夫一妻制，但它是宽宏大量的。

segments.en: Magnanimous.
segments.zh: 宏伟。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Magnanimous.
segments.zh: 宏伟。

segments.en: This is a great word.
segments.zh: 这是一个伟大的词。

segments.en: We hear this a lot in the newspaper or on TV about usually famous people.
segments.zh: 我们在报纸或电视上经常听到关于通常名人的消息。

segments.en: He did something very magnanimous or it was a magnanimous gesture.
segments.zh: 他做了一些非常宏伟的事情，或者这是一个宽宏大量的姿态。

segments.en: This describes a person who does things for the benefit of other people.
segments.zh: 这描述了为他人的利益而做事的人。

segments.en: Who is thinking about the well-being and the health and the lives of others.
segments.zh: 谁在考虑他人的健康和健康和生活。

segments.en: So it would be a person that likes to share or a person that's not selfish.
segments.zh: 所以这将是一个喜欢分享的人或一个不自私的人。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So if you donate half of your salary this month to victims of an earthquake, I would say, Marco, that's so magnanimous of you.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您本月将一半的薪水捐赠给地震的受害者，我会说，马可，您真是太宽宏了。

segments.en: You're so magnanimous.
segments.zh: 你太宽宏了。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Awesome.
segments.zh: 太棒了。

segments.en: And apart from being magnanimous, if a person is eloquent, I guess that's also a positive attribute.
segments.zh: 除了宽宏大量之外，如果一个人很有说服力，我想这也是一个积极的属性。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: This is another really good one.
segments.zh: 这是另一个非常好的。

segments.en: Someone who is eloquent is a very good speaker.
segments.zh: 雄辩的人是一个非常好的演讲者。

segments.en: This means that when they talk, they sound very, very good.
segments.zh: 这意味着当他们说话时，他们听起来非常非常好。

segments.en: Someone who's eloquent uses big words, but is also very good at making other people listen.
segments.zh: 一个雄辩的人使用大词，但也很擅长让别人听。

segments.en: So it's usually about speaking.
segments.zh: 所以通常是关于说话。

segments.en: So you would say he's an eloquent speaker.
segments.zh: 所以你会说他是一个雄辩的演讲者。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So someone who is eloquent is fun or good or interesting to listen to.
segments.zh: 所以雄辩的人很有趣、好听或有趣。

segments.en: And our last description for personalities and the way people are is a person that's daring.
segments.zh: 我们最后对个性和人们的描述是一个大胆的人。

segments.en: Well, this can be a good thing or a bad thing.
segments.zh: 好吧，这可能是好事，也可能是坏事。

segments.en: It depends on who you're talking about.
segments.zh: 这取决于你在说谁。

segments.en: Because sometimes daring people are also reckless and this can be dangerous.
segments.zh: 因为有时大胆的人也是鲁莽的，这可能很危险。

segments.en: But sometimes someone who is daring can be doing good things.
segments.zh: 但有时敢于大胆的人可能会做好事。

segments.en: Like a daring business person might take risks that other people don't take.
segments.zh: 像一个大胆的商人可能会冒其他人不承担的风险。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a person that's daring dares to take risks, right?
segments.zh: 所以敢于冒险的人，对吧？

segments.en: You are very daring.
segments.zh: 你非常大胆。

segments.en: You Marco are daring because recently you jumped out of an airplane.
segments.zh: 你马可敢，因为最近你跳下了飞机。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: You did some skydiving.
segments.zh: 你做了一些跳伞。

segments.en: So that would be considered daring.
segments.zh: 所以这将被认为是大胆的。

segments.en: That's very daring.
segments.zh: 这是非常大胆的。

segments.en: I'm not daring like that because I would never jump out of an airplane.
segments.zh: 我不敢这样，因为我永远不会跳下飞机。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we took a look at basically 10 key words here.
segments.zh: 所以我们在这里看了基本上 10 个关键词。

segments.en: A lot of adjectives, but they're a great way to describe yourself.
segments.zh: 很多形容词，但它们是描述自己的好方法。

segments.en: Maybe if you're at a job interview, sometimes a typical question is, how would you describe yourself using three adjectives?
segments.zh: 也许如果你在工作面试，有时一个典型的问题是，你会如何用三个形容词来形容自己？

segments.en: I'm extroverted, I'm diligent, and I'm open-minded.
segments.zh: 我性格外向，我很勤奋，我思想开放。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That's awesome.
segments.zh: 太棒了。

segments.en: See?
segments.zh: 看到了吧？

segments.en: You sound really professional when you say things like this.
segments.zh: 当你说这样的话时，你听起来真的很专业。

segments.en: Give me the job.
segments.zh: 给我工作。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So and even if you took a look at some of the negative adjectives that we used, it's also a typical job interview question is like, what are your biggest faults?
segments.zh: 所以即使你看了一些我们使用的负面形容词，这也是一个典型的求职面试问题，你最大的缺点是什么？

segments.en: So you can say, well, maybe I am superstitious and naive.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，好吧，也许我是迷信和天真的。

segments.en: You wouldn't want to say that in a job interview.
segments.zh: 你不会想在求职面试中这么说。

segments.en: But I mean, I don't know, maybe.
segments.zh: 但我的意思是，我不知道，也许。

segments.en: Because you have to say something, right?
segments.zh: 因为你必须说点什么，对吧？

segments.en: You do.
segments.zh: 确实得说点什么。

segments.en: But I would say, sometimes I'm a bit too daring or sometimes I take things personally.
segments.zh: 但我会说，有时我有点太大胆了，或者有时我会把事情个人化。

segments.en: So we can talk about that another time.
segments.zh: 所以我们可以再谈一次。

segments.en: But I think for now, it'd be good if we listened to today's dialogue one more time and really got a good sense of how to use these words.
segments.zh: 但我认为，如果我们再听一次今天的对话，并且真正了解如何使用这些词，那就太好了。

segments.en: Okay, class, settle down.
segments.zh: 好吧，上课，安定下来。

segments.en: I have the results of your individual personality tests.
segments.zh: 我有你个人性格测试的结果。

segments.en: I am going to hand them out.
segments.zh: 我要把它们分发。

segments.en: And if you'd like, you can read them out loud to the rest of the class.
segments.zh: 如果您愿意，您可以将它们大声朗读给班上的其他人。

segments.en: I'll read mine.
segments.zh: 我会读我的。

segments.en: Okay, go ahead.
segments.zh: 好的，继续。

segments.en: It says here that I am adventurous, outgoing, and easygoing.
segments.zh: 它在这里说我喜欢冒险、外向和随和。

segments.en: It says that I'm a little superstitious and occasionally naive.
segments.zh: 它说我有点迷信，偶尔也很天真。

segments.en: That's not true.
segments.zh: 那不是真的。

segments.en: Well, the test isn't 100% accurate.
segments.zh: 好吧，测试不是 100% 准确的。

segments.en: Is that all it says?
segments.zh: 这就是它所说的一切吗？

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: It also says that I'm open-minded with great ambition, but that I can also be reckless and clumsy.
segments.zh: 它还说我心胸开阔，雄心勃勃，但我也可以鲁莽和笨拙。

segments.en: This is stupid.
segments.zh: 这太蠢了。

segments.en: Okay, anyone else want to read theirs?
segments.zh: 好吧，还有人想读他们的吗？

segments.en: I'll go.
segments.zh: 我会去的。

segments.en: It says that I'm an extroverted, well-balanced person.
segments.zh: 它说我是一个外向、平衡良好的人。

segments.en: It says I am generous, outspoken, and very diligent.
segments.zh: 它说我很慷慨，直言不讳，非常勤奋。

segments.en: This is so true.
segments.zh: 这是真的。

segments.en: It also says that I am a magnanimous, eloquent, and daring.
segments.zh: 它还说我是一个宽宏大量的、雄辩的、大胆的。

segments.en: This is totally me.
segments.zh: 这完全是我。

segments.en: Whatever.
segments.zh: 随便吧。

segments.en: These tests are baloney.
segments.zh: 这些测试是胡说八道。

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now going into descriptions.
segments.zh: 所以现在进入描述。

segments.en: What are three adjectives that you would use to describe someone that you hate the most?
segments.zh: 你会用哪三个形容词来形容你最讨厌的人？

segments.en: So going back to describing people, how would you describe one of the main things that really irritate you about someone?
segments.zh: 所以回到描述人的描述，你会如何描述让你真正恼火的人之一？

segments.en: Maybe if they are clumsy, it really bothers you that people are clumsy or reckless maybe.
segments.zh: 也许如果他们笨拙，人们可能很笨拙或鲁莽，这真的会让你感到困扰。

segments.en: I see what you're saying.
segments.zh: 我明白你在说什么。

segments.en: Well, I really like extroverted, hardworking people, but in English we have a word to describe someone who is too extroverted, too hardworking.
segments.zh: 嗯，我真的很喜欢外向、勤奋的人，但在英语中，我们有一个词来形容一个太外向、太努力的人。

segments.en: We call this person a type A personality.
segments.zh: 我们称这个人为 A 型人格。

segments.en: Type A. Type A.
segments.zh: A型。类型A。

segments.en: The letter A. And this means someone who works very, very hard, who is very, very serious, but who's always anxious, always needs to get things done.
segments.zh: 字母 A. 这意味着工作非常非常努力，非常非常认真，但总是很焦虑，总是需要把事情做好的人。

segments.en: And so these people can be very hard to work with because they're controlling and they're never calm.
segments.zh: 所以这些人可能很难相处，因为他们控制不住，而且他们永远不会冷静。

segments.en: So they're not easygoing.
segments.zh: 所以他们并不随和。

segments.en: No, they're not easygoing.
segments.zh: 不，它们并不随和。

segments.en: They always want to do what they want to do.
segments.zh: 他们总是想做他们想做的事。

segments.en: They're usually not very good listeners.
segments.zh: 他们通常不是很好的听众。

segments.en: And so this type A personality is something that I would say I'm not a big fan of at work or even when we're going out because with friends, it's hard to be around someone who always has to control you.
segments.zh: 所以这种 A 型个性是我会说我不是工作中的忠实粉丝，甚至在我们要出去的时候，因为和朋友在一起，很难和一个总是必须控制你的人在一起。

segments.en: This is very interesting.
segments.zh: 这很有趣。

segments.en: And I'm sure our listeners have a lot of different ways to describe things that irritate them, maybe about people or maybe attributes that they really admire about someone.
segments.zh: 我敢肯定，我们的听众有很多不同的方式来描述让他们恼火的事物，也许是关于人，或者可能是他们真正钦佩某人的属性。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And I want to give everybody a little bit of homework today.
segments.zh: 我今天想给大家一点功课。

segments.en: Go home or if you're at home, look up a word in the dictionary that describes yourself.
segments.zh: 回家或者如果你在家，在字典中查找描述自己的单词。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: An adjective to describe yourself.
segments.zh: 形容自己的形容词。

segments.en: I think this is a really good homework assignment because you'll be improving your vocabulary and then put it on our website, EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 我认为这是一个非常好的家庭作业，因为您将提高您的词汇量，然后将其放在我们的网站 englishpod.com 上。

segments.en: Let us know more about you.
segments.zh: 让我们更多地了解您。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We'll see everyone there.
segments.zh: 到时候见，各位。

segments.en: Bye everyone.
segments.zh: 大家再见。
